Prospects Traded at the 2026 Deadline

August 10, 2026 Tony Bps General, MiLB 0

Tweet
Share
Pin
0 Shares
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 21:50
Instaread

As with every trade deadline, many prospects were moved in deals. It may take a few years to decide who were the winners of the deals, but that’s in the future. The fun part is seeing who got moved where and for whom. For those in AL/NL only leagues, quite a few players switched leagues which means you can get a jump on the better prospects if they are not already owned.

Pitcher were in high demand and cost more in prospects than in previous seasons, but with so many teams looking to load up for the postseason run, it was definitely a seller’s market. The preseason ranks are, obviously, months old and most of these players will go up or down in our next organization prospect rankings.


A few interesting facts about the prospects traded this deadline –
-The sons of four former major leaguers were traded – Benny Agbayani, Eliezer Alfonzo, Mark McGwire and Jeff Kent
– A Hope and a Hoppe were traded, along with 3 Smiths, 2 Cruz’s, 2 Moores and 2 Santanas along with a Hill and a Gill Hill
– There was a biblical theme of players moved – an Angel, a Moises, a Jacob, a Josiah, a Jacob, a Mark, a Luke and a John. Why couldn’t the Phillies have traded Matthew Fisher? A River was also parted with.

Okay, on to the players now all listed in alphabetical order below.

Mason Adams, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 20
From: Chicago White Sox
To: Colorado Rockies
For: Brenton Doyle, OF
Adams doesn’t have the best offerings but could start for Colorado as soon as this season.

Bruin Agbayani, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 42
From: Minnesota Twins
To: New York Mets
For: A.J. Minter, LHP
The son of Mets legend, Benny, hasn’t played much because of injuries and is still very young at 19 years old so he’s likely a few years away from the majors. Being in the same organization where his father was revered could give him more chances to become a major leaguer.

Omar Alfonzo, C
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 22
From: Pittsburgh Pirates
To: New York Yankees
For: Camilo Doval, RHP
The Yankees have had a catcher problem all year but this move doesn’t change the trajectory for Alonzo much. He’s more of a future backup than a regular regardless of the team he’s on.

Billy Amick, 3B
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 16
From: Minnesota Twins
To: New York Mets
For: A.J. Minter, LHP
Amick has good power but has dealt with injuries in the past and hasn’t shown a great hit-tool yet. Perhaps a change of scenery could help him develop. He’s 23 years old and could make a move to the majors later this season as the Mets see what they have for the future.

Angel Arredondo, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Texas Rangers
To: Los Angeles Angels
For: Logan O’Hoppe, C & Chase Silseth, RHP
Arrendono is more valuble in real life than in fantasy, being a defensive-minded player with little pop or speed. He can get on base but doesn’t provide much else. This trade will get him to the major leagues quicker with an Angels team desperate for any success it could find.

Enddy Azocar, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 15
From: Boston Red Sox
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Adley Rutschman, C
Good pop and putting up solid numbers for a teenager.

Moises Ballesteros, C
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 1
From: Chicago Cubs
To: Los Angeles Angels
For: Ryan Zeferjahn, RHP
Ballesteros struggled after his first month but has the potential to develop into a solid hitter with power for the Angels.

Zane Barnhart, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Baltimore Orioles
To: Detroit Tigers
For: Jake Rogers, C
Barnhart is a middle reliever who won’t make much of an impact if he makes the majors.

Brett Bateman, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 27
From: Chicago Cubs
To: Toronto Blue Jays
For: Kevin Gausman, RHP
Old school type of player who draws walks, hits singles with little power.

Jace Beck, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Chicago Cubs
To: Miami Marlins
For: Braxton Garrett, LHP
Beck could have an impact on Miami’s bullpen this season as a source of holds.

Brandan Bidois, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Pittsburgh Pirates
To: Miami Marlins
For: Lake Bachar, RHP
Future middle reliever potentially in Miami.

Lucas Braun, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 13
From: Atlanta Braves
To: Kansas City Royals
For: Lane Thomas, OF & Bailey Falter, LHP
Braun is a crafty-type pitcher without a great fastball or put-away pitch and could be a 4th or 5th starter type in the majors. He has a better chance at making the majors on the Royals who should have some openings next season.

Jack Cebert, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 47
From: New York Yankees
To: Washington Nationals
For: Luis Garcia Jr.

Jacob Cozart, C
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 27
From: Cleveland Guardians
To: Los Angeles Angels
For: Jo Adell, OF
Cozart has some pop from behind the plate but has a poor hitting tool. He could develop into a backup role due to his solid defense.

Luis Cruz, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Pittsburgh Pirates
To: New York Yankees
For: Camilo Doval, RHP
Cruz has put up solid numbers as a teenage in the Pirates low minors and could develop into a solid player as he gains more experience.

Yovanny Cruz, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: New York Yankees
To: Washington Nationals
For: Luis Garcia Jr.
Cruz may step right into a weak Nationals bullpen right away and could surprise some with holds and even potentially saves.

Gabe Davis, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 39
From: Chicago White Sox
To: New York Mets
For: Huascar Brazoban, RHP
Davis is a potential reliever with command issues.

Duncan Davitt, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Chicago White Sox
To: Atlanta Braves
For: Joey Bart, C
Organizational fodder type.

Will Dion, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Cleveland Guardians
To: Washington Nationals
For: Foster Griffin, LHP
Dion could be a part of a weak Nationals bullpen as soon as this season.

Felix Doroteo, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Chicago White Sox
To: Pittsburgh Pirates
For: Jose Urquidy, RHP
Doroteo is a middle relief prospect who has control issues. This trade doesn’t change his future impact much.

Carlos Duran, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Los Angeles Dodgers
To: Kansas City Royals
For: Kris Bubic, LHP
Duran could step into Kansas City’s bullpen right away.

Daniel Eagen, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 12
From: Arizona Diamondbacks
To: St. Louis Cardinals
For: Lars Nootbar, OF
Eagen could be a back-end rotation starter if he continues to develop.

Anthony Eyanson, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 10
From: Boston Red Sox
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Adley Rutschman, C
This could be the ace that Baltimore has long needed as soon as next season.

Michael Forret, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 12
From: Tampa Bay Rays
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Tyler Wells, RHP
Forret could be a mid-rotation starter for Baltimore as soon as next year.

Zach Franklin, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 35
From: Chicago White Sox
To: New York Mets
For: Huascar Brazoban, RHP
Organization fodder-type.

Alexander Frias, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Milwaukee Brewers
To: St. Louis Cardinals
For: JoJo Romero, LHP & Dustin May, RHP
A toolsy young outfielder who could develop into a solid contributor

Luke Gabrysh, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Philadelphia Phillies
To: New York Mets
For: Brooks Raley, LHP
Organizational-type of starter with limited control to impact a major league team.

Marty Gair, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Philadelphia Phillies
To: New York Mets
For: Luis Arraez, 2B & Caleb Killian, RHP
Gair has immense strikeout ability but his command isn’t his strongest suit. Could help with saves and holds in another year or two.

Joe Glassey, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Baltimore Orioles
To: Washington Nationals
For: Christian Franklin, OF
Glassey could be a bullpen piece in the future if all goes well.

Ben Grable, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: New York Yankees
To: Washington Nationals
For: Luis Garcia Jr.
Reliever with high velocity who could move quickly to the majors.

Josh Hartle, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 19
From: Cleveland Guardians
To: Washington Nationals
For: Foster Griffin, LHP
Hartle is a potential mid-rotation type if he continue his development.

Joniel Hernandez, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: San Diego Padres
To: San Francisco Giants
For: Robbie Ray, LHP
Hernandez is young but has the tools to develop into a contributor.

Gary Gill Hill, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 19
From: Tampa Bay Rays
To: New York Mets
For: Freddy Peralta, RHP
Hill could continue to develop in a Mets organization that isn’t as successful as the Rays in turning out pitchers but they have done well with some of them. Hill has struggled this season but maybe a change of scenery could help?

Dasan Hill, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 6
From: Minnesota Twins
To: Toronto Blue Jays
For: Jeff Hoffman, RHP
Hill has the potential to be a solid mid-rotation starter for Toronto.

Carter Holton, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 24
From: Atlanta Braves
To: Kansas City Royals
For: Lane Thomas, OF & Bailey Falter, LHP
Holton missed all of 2025 with an injury but has been healthy this season and probably won’t see major league time for another year or so.

Zyhir Hope, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 3
From: Los Angeles Dodgers
To: Detroit Tigers
For: Tarik Skubal, LHP
Hope has a clearer path to the major leagues after this deal. Even though Detroit isn’t in rebuild move they have shown they aren’t afraid to give playing time to younger players and Hope could see time in the majors as soon as next year if he keeps hitting. Hope brings a great skillset having hit for power with a high average and OBP in the minors.

Alex Hoppe, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Seattle Mariners
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Taylor Ward, OF
Hoppe struggled somewhat in the majors so far but has good stuff and may be a part of Seattle’s bullpen going forward.

Kaeden Kent, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 15
From: New York Yankees
To: San Francisco Giants
For: Heliot Ramos, OF
Kent has the potential to be a utility player in the major leagues.

Jacob Kisting, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Tampa Bay Rays
To: Miami Marlins
For: Liam Hicks, C/1B
Future 5th starter type.

John Klein, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 33
From: Minnesota Twins
To: Toronto Blue Jays
For: Jeff Hoffman, RHP
Klein could have a future role in Toronto’s bullpen.

Harrison Kreiling, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Seattle Mariners
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Taylor Ward, OF
Potential reliever.

Henry Lalane, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 9
From: New York Yankees
To: San Francisco Giants
For: Heliot Ramos, OF
Lalane is bouncing back after an injury last season. Could be a solid part of the rotation in the near future.

Hyun Seung Lee, MI
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Pittsburgh Pirates
To: Miami Marlins
For: Lake Bachar, RHP
Lee is struggling this season after a solid 2025 but is years away.

Jonathon Long, 1B
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 5
From: Chicago Cubs
To: Miami Marlins
For: Braxton Garrett, LHP
This trade frees Long from a packed Chicago lineup to a Miami team to give him a much clearer path to the major leagues. Could be a sneaky source of power.

Mark Manfredi, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Milwaukee Brewers
To: Colorado Rockies
For: Antonio Senzetela, RHP
Potential middle reliever for Colorado but the key word here is Colorado so buyer beware.

Ramon Marquez, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 20
From: Philadelphia Phillies
To: New York Mets
For: Luis Arraez, 2B & Caleb Killian, RHP
Marquez would have ranked much higher in the midseason top 50 if he remained in the organization after a spectacular season. He has shown mid-rotation or better potential and should move up quickly in San Francisco.

Juan Martinez, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Milwaukee Brewers
To: Colorado Rockies
For: Antonio Senzetela, RHP
Martinez tore up Rookie Ball but struggled in Low-A so far. He’s a toolsy prospect but very young. In Colorado, it could be worth a gamble to see if he develops.

Aiden May, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 38
From: Miami Marlins
To: Colorado Rockies
For: Victor Vodnik, RHP
May could be a back-end rotation starter but faces long odds in Colorado.

Kash Mayfield, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 2
From: San Diego Padres
To: Detroit Tigers
For: Casey Mize, RHP
Mayfield has the potential to be a real solid starter in the majors as he gains experience.

Chayce McDermott, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Baltimore: 42
From: Los Angeles Dodgers
To: New York Mets
For: Ben Rortvedt, C
McDermott has bounced around to a few teams and could get a chance in the bullpen for the Mets this season.

Mason McGwire, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Chicago Cubs
To: Los Angeles Angels
For: Ryan Zeferjahn, RHP
McGwire could develop into a solid bullpen piece for the Angels

Miguel Mendez, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 4
From: San Diego Padres
To: San Francisco Giants
For: Robbie Ray, LHP
Mendez has been solid and could appear in the majors very soon and has the makings of a mid-rotation starter.

Eddie Micheletti, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Toronto Blue Jays
To: Los Angeles Angels
For: Jose Soriano, RHP
Potential backup outfielder/bench player type with some power.

Nick Mitchell, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 44
From: Cleveland Guardians
To: Washington Nationals
For: Foster Griffin, LHP
Mitchell looks to be a 4th outfielder type if he continues to develop.

Andrew Moore, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: San Diego Padres
To: Pittsburgh Pirates
For: Hunter Stratton, RHP
Organizational depth type.

Brock Moore, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Seattle Mariners
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Taylor Ward, OF
A hard-throwing reliver with some command issues.

Arjun Nimmala, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 4
From: Toronto Blue Jays
To: Los Angeles Angels
For: Jose Soriano, RHP
Solid Top-50 prospect with good hitting tool along with developing power.

Dameury Pena, 2B
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 29
From: Minnesota Twins
To: Toronto Blue Jays
For: Jeff Hoffman, RHP
Pena has a solid hit-tool with a little speed but no power.

Emilien Pitre, 2B
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 32
From: Tampa Bay Rays
To: New York Mets
For: Freddy Peralta, RHP
Pitre could help the Mets in a future role as a utility player maybe as soon as next season.

Josiah Ragsdale, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Milwaukee Brewers
To: St. Louis Cardinals
For: JoJo Romero, LHP & Dustin May, RHP
Projects to be a 4th outfielder/bench type but perhaps St. Louis could coax more out of him.

Jhomnardo Reyes, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Minnesota Twins
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Dean Kremer, RHP
Reyes is only 18 years old but put up impressive numbers in the FCL and, while he’s years away, the Baltimore organization has done a solid job of developing young talent. He’s actually a player to keep an eye on from this list.

Alejandro Rivera, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Cleveland Guardians
To: Cincinnati Reds
For: Nathanial Lowe, 1B
Rivera is a lottery ticket who’s shown good numbers in the low minors so far.

Angel Rivero, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Toronto Blue Jays
To: Los Angeles Angels
For: Jose Soriano, RHP
Young lottery ticket starting pitcher.

Kyle Robinson, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Los Angeles Angels
To: Pittsburgh Pirates
For: Kyle Robinson, RHP
Robinson could be a back-end rotation starter in the majors.

Jefferson Rojas, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 4
From: Chicago Cubs
To: New York Mets
For: Clay Holmes, RHP & Tyrone Taylor, OF
Rojas could be part of a dynamic young Mets team as soon as next year if he continues his development.

River Ryan, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 16
From: Los Angeles Dodgers
To: Detroit Tigers
For: Tarik Skubal, LHP
Ryan has a much clearer path to a starting rotation with Detroit than the Dodgers. For a Tigers team that is still looking to contend (even after this deal), Ryan could step in as soon as September. He has the makings of a solid mid-rotation type.

Brian Sanchez, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Pittsburgh Pirates
To: Miami Marlins
For: Lake Bachar, RHP
Sanchez is a potential backup outfielder type.

Adrian Santana, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 24
From: Tampa Bay Rays
To: Miami Marlins
For: Liam Hicks, C/1B
Speedy shortstop with good defensive skills.

Sandro Santana, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Arizona Diamondbacks
To: St. Louis Cardinals
For: Lars Nootbar, OF
Santana has the potential to be a solid member of the bullpen in the future.

Aidan Smith, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 5
From: Tampa Bay Rays
To: New York Mets
For: Freddy Peralta, RHP
Smith struggled this season after a solid 2025 with the Rays. Perhaps the Mets can help him rediscover some of that magic?

Boston Smith, C
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Chicago White Sox
To: Seattle Mariners
For: Luis Castillo, RHP
Smith could appear quicker in the major leagues with the Mariners, a team more desperate for offense than the White Sox. While Seattle has Cal Raleigh behind the plate, his struggles this year have been well-known. Like Raleigh, Smith has massive power with strikeout issues but draws walks and could add some pop into the Seattle lineup as early as next season.

Brady Smith, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50:43
From: Los Angeles Dodgers
To: Detroit Tigers
For: Tarik Skubal, LHP
Smith is a couple of years away from the majors, only having less than 100 innings pitched in his career, because of injuries. When healthy, he has put up quality numbers with good strikeout potential. As with Hope and Ryan, Smith would have a clearer path to the majors with Detroit, when he’s ready.

Ty Southisene, 2B
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 17
From: Chicago Cubs
To: Toronto Blue Jays
For: Kevin Gausman, RHP
Potential utility type player with little to no power but a solid hit tool.

John Spikerman, OF
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 29
From: Philadelphia Phillies
To: New York Mets
For: Brooks Raley, LHP
Potential leadoff type if he can continue to develop. Does not offer much in the way of power but can steal a base.

Sammy Stafura, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 11
From: Pittsburgh Pirates
To: New York Mets
For: Luke Weaver, RHP
Having a real solid season, Stafura could put himself in the running for a MI spot in New York soon.

Brayden Taylor, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 31
From: Tampa Bay Rays
To: Miami Marlins
For: Liam Hicks, C/1B
Taylor was a former 1st round pick who hasn’t put it all together yet.

Carlos Vielma, SS
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: Chicago White Sox
To: Colorado Rockies
For: Brenton Doyle, OF
Recent free agent signing is years away from the major leagues but goes to the best hitters park in the game.

Kendeglys Virguez, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 49
From: Cleveland Guardians
To: Washington Nationals
For: Foster Griffin, LHP
Virquez has big-time strikeout stuff but poor control. His odds of success lessen in the move out of the Cleveland pitching factory, though.

Kyson Witherspoon, RHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: 4
From: Boston Red Sox
To: Baltimore Orioles
For: Adley Rutschman, C
Potential mid-rotation starter for a Baltimore team that is seems is always looking for pitching.

Jackson Wolf, LHP
Rank On Team’s Preseason Top 50: Unranked
From: San Diego Padres
To: Detroit Tigers
For: Casey Mize, RHP
Middle reliver potential who could get a chance in the less-than-stellar Detroit bullpen.
